simple.meaning: מִקְרֶה (miqreh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ruth 2:3. The surrounding context includes family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִקְרֶה (H4745) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מִקְרֶה (miqreh) / H4745 is traced through Ruth 2:3, 1 Samuel 6:9, 1 Samuel 20:26, Ecclesiastes 2:14 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H4745. miqreh מִקְרֶה noun masculine 1Sam 6:9 accident, chance, fortune ; — absolute ׳מ 6:9 +; construct מִקְרֵה Eccl 2:15 (so read also 3:19 (twice in verse) with ᵐ5 Ruët Kau Wild, for מִקְרֶה ᵑ0 ); — 1 accident, chance , 1Sam 6:9 ; 20:26 ; with קָרָה Ruth 2:2 (see ׳ק 1 ). 2 in Ecclesiastes, fortune, fate , אֶתכֻּֿלָּם יִקְרֶה אֶחָד ׳מ Eccl 2:14 compare 2:15 , 3:19 (3 t. in verse); 9:2-3 ,.
